messages.message: Tactical DNA describes the club's preferred playing style. It assesses how well the squad fits that style, influences team chemistry and has a small effect on match simulation.
The database columns for tactical DNA are still missing. Please run the SQL update first.
Changing style can improve chemistry if the new style fits the squad better. If the fit is poor, chemistry decreases and only recovers through matches or a more suitable style.
The assistant manager recommends switching to {style}. Squad fit would be {fit}%, which is {diff} points higher.
The staff currently sees no compelling reason to change style.
Without an assistant manager, there is no staff recommendation for tactical DNA.
Tactical DNA saved: {style}. Squad fit: {fit}%. Chemistry effect: {chemistry}.
Tactical DNA saved: {style}. Squad fit: {fit}%. The transition initially harms chemistry ({chemistry}).
Tactical DNA updated. No style change required.
You are not allowed to change this club's tactical DNA.
Tactical DNA has only a small effect in matches and mainly rewards a good fit between style, squad, training and staff.
Neutral style without strict specialisation. Base strength, technique, stamina, passing, tackling and freshness are weighted evenly.
Stamina, pace, tackling and mentality increase the effect of this high-intensity style.
Passing, creativity and technique help control the game.
Tackling, heading, stamina and influential players strengthen a compact defensive style.
Overall strength, heading, stamina and tackling make this style more effective.
Pace, finishing, passing and freshness are especially well suited to quick transitions.
Your squad is very well suited to this style.
Your squad is reasonably well suited to this style.
This style is currently only partly suited to your squad.
{team} changes its tactical DNA from {oldstyle} to {newstyle}. Current squad fit is {fit}%, with a direct chemistry effect of {chemistry}.
